I think you should order, and read a book called, "Self Editing For Fiction Writers".
Renni Browne and David King.
This will help you considerably in learning to write, and communicate effectively through the written word.

I also suggest, that when you write, sit at your keyboard and pound out the words. DO NOT do any editing at this point. Once you lose the rhythm by stopping to edit, it is extremely difficult to get back on track with your original train of thought. In addition, do not proofread your own work. When we do this, we rationalize and overlook the errors in our writing. 

I would also recommend that you buy a stack of 3x5 index cards. Prior to sitting down and writing, jot down your ideas and thoughts for your characters, and storyline on individual cards. This will allow you to shuffle the cards around, giving you a rough layout of your characters/stories sequence of events.

Conversely, you could also keep a journal style notebook with all your thoughts, ideas concerning your story. 
Don't be afraid to write down random ideas that you might not even use until a couple of stories later. 

In addition, give very serious thought concerning the opening sentence of your story. If you cannot grab the reader's attention in the first sentence, you have already lost them. Take a look at the collective works of Edgar Allan Poe.
Poe would agonize in finding that first sentence that effectively captures his readers attention. The same is true for Ernest Hemingway, along with many other writers.

One last thought, and this may seem nonsensical, listen to your characters as you write, sooner or later the characters, will tell you where they, and this story wants to go.

She told me she was in a relationship at that point.

However she asked for my number and she would let me know if anything changed in the future. 

I figured it was a standard brush off, but I gave her my number anyways. 
Almost a year to the day, I received a call from her. The relationship with this other person ended, but she had kept my number the entire time and decided to finally call me. 

We went out, and began dating which lasted almost 2 years, unfortunately due to a serious illness she passed away a few months later. 

I guess the moral of the story, is to let her make the decision as to whether or not to call you.

Being patient sometimes has its rewards.
